proposals.before: The rhetorician Cao Qiusheng traded on influence for gold, curried favor with men such as the favorite Zhao Tan, and was close to Dou Zhang, the empress's brother.
proposals.after: The rhetorician Cao Qiusheng traded on influence for gold, curried favor with men such as the favorite Zhao Tan, and was close to Dou Zhangjun.
proposals.reason: Chinese 與竇長君善 does not identify Dou as the empress's brother; that kinship is an invention.

proposals.before: Then he traveled to Luoyang to see Xiahou Ying, the Marquis of Ru-yin, and argued, "What wrong has Ji Bu done?
proposals.after: Then he traveled to Luoyang to see the Marquis of Ruyin, Lord Teng, and argued, "What wrong has Ji Bu done?
proposals.reason: Chinese has only 汝陰侯滕公; the personal name Xiahou Ying is not in the source sentence.

proposals.before: When Peng Yue was a commoner family man, he once roamed with Bu; in poverty and straits, he sold labor in Qi and was a wine-shop guarantor.
proposals.after: When Peng Yue was a commoner family man, he once roamed with Bu; in poverty and straits, they hired out labor in Qi, and Bu was a wine-shop guard.
proposals.reason: 為酒家保 refers to Luan Bu in parallel with the idiomatic reading, not Peng Yue alone as the tavern guarantor.

proposals.before: Xiahou Ying knew Zhu Jia for a famous man of chivalry and guessed Ji Bu lay hidden with him; he agreed to speak.
proposals.after: Lord Teng knew Zhu Jia for a famous man of chivalry and guessed Ji Bu lay hidden with him; he agreed to speak.
proposals.reason: Chinese subject is 滕公; Xiahou Ying is not stated in this sentence.

decisions.after: The rhetorician Cao Qiusheng repeatedly cultivated influence and sought money, attached himself to prominent men such as Zhao Tan, and befriended Dou Changjun, the empress's elder brother.
decisions.reason: The proposal correctly repairs Dou Zhang but wrongly discards a valid identification. Shiji 49 explicitly identifies Dou Changjun as Empress Dou's elder brother.
Marquis of Ruyin and Lord Teng identify Xiahou Ying. Expanding a title to his established personal name is accurate and improves continuity rather than inventing a person.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 初嬰為滕令奉車，故號滕公

decisions.after: When Peng Yue was a commoner family man, he once roamed with Bu; in poverty and straits, they hired out labor in Qi, and Bu was a wine-shop guarantor.
decisions.reason: 窮困，賣庸於齊，為酒家保 is shared hardship with Bu, and 為酒家保 belongs to Bu (as the parallel idiomatic already has); the proposed 'wine-shop guard' misrenders 保, so keep 'guarantor' while correcting the agent.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 窮困，賣庸於齊，為酒家保

decisions.reason: Lord Teng is Xiahou Ying. Retaining his personal name is an accurate explanatory identification and keeps the actor clear across the passage.
